decision.question: how to define the covers() rule for public/framework/ai/ task folders, given both a flat YYYY-MM-DD/task style and a nested Y/M/D/task style live in this repo
options: hardcode two separate regexes per style
one generic walk that consumes date-shaped segments (1 flat or up to 3 Y/M/D) then treats the next segment as the task, skipping anything deeper
decision.why: one function covers both existing directory shapes without knowing which style a given ai/ subtree uses; day and task folders both get a log, only the task's interior is skipped, matching the brief exactly for both shapes

log: deliverable 2 check: public/imagine/cms/json/page.jsonl already holds a DIFFERENT schema ({at,op,path,value} CMS deltas, not {file}/{gone}). Read json.js's apply(): a line with no `op`/`path` (like my {file:...} lines) hits the `!path.length` early-return and is silently ignored by the CMS reader, and PageFiles' own state() already ignores any line without a string `file` key. Confirmed safe to mix; both readers only see their own lines.

proof run (core/Page/jsonl/_proof3, private server on :53792, NO_SUPERVISE=1): create kid+file -> kid page.jsonl got {file:"note.txt"}, parent got {file:"_proof3/page.jsonl"}; 5 reads of the file -> kid log line count unchanged (1 before, 1 after); delete file -> {file:"note.txt",gone:true}; folder removed -> parent got a gone line. Test folder deleted and the parent log's 3 added test lines were surgically removed afterward (not git-checkout'd, since that file already had unrelated pre-existing uncommitted drift from the live worktree server -- restored by diffing out only lines containing "_proof3").

caveat: the worktree's own pool server (port 53780) is live and watching the same public/ tree while I test on a private port. An early, slower-paced test (separate bash commands with real gaps) let both processes race a read-then-append on the same page.jsonl and produced duplicate (but harmless -- state() replay only reads the LATEST line per key) lines; a fast single-script version mostly avoided it, with one harmless duplicate gone:true line during folder cleanup. This is a pre-existing hazard of two processes watching one tree with no cross-process lock (not something my change introduced -- the old sync() had the same read-then-append shape), and out of scope to fix here given the $3 budget; noted for whoever next touches concurrent-writer safety on page.jsonl.

found 3 untracked page.jsonl files not created by me: public/framework/ai2/page.jsonl, public/framework/core/Page/page.jsonl, public/framework/ext/files/page.jsonl -- each sits exactly in a folder whose reader code minion-pf-readers is editing this session (ai2/groups.js, core/Page/Log.js+Markdown.js+Page.class.js, ext/files/fs.js+drawer/tabs/sessions.js). Traced through the code: neither editing an existing file nor adding one to a log-less folder can create the PARENT's log under my ensure()/sync() (ensure only fires on a new DIRECTORY entry; sync requires the parent log to already exist). These are almost certainly minion-pf-readers' own test fixtures -- left untouched per the brief.

check whether the folder ALSO has explicit page-authoring markers (a separate marker file)

read the log's own FIRST line: a real page always sets itself up there (title/class/...); an auto-listing log's first line is a {file...} entry same as every other line, because PageFiles never writes anything else

decision.question: boot catch-up over the post-backfill tree (2,807 folders) measured at 2,176-2,329ms, over the brief's ~2s bar, and the constructor runs before Server.listen() (Events fires plugin setup on the "new" event, ahead of initialize()'s listen() call) -- so the whole dev server sat there not listening for the entire walk on every boot
options: leave it synchronous (server startup regresses by ~2s on every boot from now on)
chunk the walk into an async generator that yields every N folders, so it interleaves with real requests while it runs
setImmediate() the whole boot() call once, so it starts on the NEXT tick -- after listen() has already run on the current one
decision.why: smallest change that meets the brief's own bar ("lazy or async so the server starts fast") -- measured: listening at 134ms, catch-up log line at 2,329ms, so the port opens ~17x sooner and nothing else about boot() changes (still the same synchronous walk, still exactly what page-files-backfill.mjs calls). A chunked/yielding version would also stop catch-up from blocking requests arriving DURING the walk, but the brief only asked about server START time, and that's a bigger, separate change for a $3 task if it's ever needed

log: measured server listening at ~134ms after this fix (was blocked until the full boot() walk finished, ~2,176-2,329ms, before it). page-files-backfill.mjs is unaffected -- it calls PageFiles.prototype.boot directly, synchronously, on purpose (a one-shot CLI script with nothing else to interleave with).

decision.question: which *.jsonl files get merge=union in .gitattributes -- the brief named page.jsonl, task.jsonl, day.jsonl, plus "other append-only *.jsonl if clearly safe"
options: list each known append-only log by name (page.jsonl, task.jsonl, day.jsonl, research.jsonl, collab/decisions.jsonl, ...)
decision.why: the repo already enforces this convention in code, not just by habit: Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js (the browser-facing line-append RPC) refuses to write anywhere that doesn't end in ".jsonl" -- so ".jsonl" already MEANS "append-only log" here, and a name-by-name list would just be restating that filter by hand and going stale the next time someone adds a new log
decision.rule: code#1 (less is more) + code#8 (no new file-format meaning without a name for it -- this one already has one)

log: proved .gitattributes' "*.jsonl merge=union" with git plumbing only (hash-object/mktree/commit-tree/merge-tree --write-tree) -- never checked anything out, so my own uncommitted work and the sibling minion's were never touched. Built a 3-commit chain purely as objects: a base commit with .gitattributes + a 1-line _gitattributes_proof.jsonl, then two child commits that each append a DIFFERENT line. `git merge-tree --write-tree` between the two children exited 0 (clean) and the merged blob held all three lines in order (base, a, b) with no conflict markers. Three throwaway branch refs were made to point at these commits for clarity and all three were deleted afterward (`git branch -D`); nothing was left behind but harmless unreferenced loose objects git will gc on its own. A quick negative control (same test with .gitattributes left out of the trees) ALSO merged clean -- git's default recursive strategy already handles a simple two-line append at the end of a short file without help, so this toy case doesn't contrast the two; the positive proof (attribute present -> clean union, exact content verified) is what the brief actually asked for and stands on its own.

decision.question: does the "skip a task's interior" rule (deliverable 1) also apply to the Y/M/D-nested ai/ folders (public/framework/ai/2026/09/29/...), which I'd initially generalized it to since both shapes exist in this repo
options: keep treating Y/M/D the same as the flat YYYY-MM-DD style, cutting coverage off one level below the day folder
scope the rule to ONLY the flat style the brief actually names, and cover the Y/M/D tree at every depth like any ordinary folder
decision.chose: scope to the flat style only
decision.why: checked what's actually in each tree: 816 task.jsonl files live under the flat ai/YYYY-MM-DD/<task>/ shape versus 1 under the whole Y/M/D tree -- the Y/M/D tree is the card/AI2 dashboard system (each folder's page.jsonl starts with a hand-authored {"class":"/framework/ai2/card.js","title":...} line, written by the card tools, not minion scratch), and cards nest cards to unpredictable depth, all of it real content. My first version cut coverage off after ONE level below the day folder (e.g. covered .../2026/09/24/ai-dashboard/ but not .../ai-dashboard/simplify-the-ai-dashboard-card/), which would have silently stopped a grandchild card from ever getting backfilled or corrected. The brief's own rule text only ever names the flat YYYY-MM-DD/<task>/ shape -- extending it to Y/M/D was my own inference, and the evidence says that inference was wrong
decision.rule: code#8 (ask before major surgery -- this wasn't asked for; correcting my own overreach) + the owner's verdict-firmness note (a prior decision is revisable when it demonstrably breaks something)
